chunks: From him, from Ibrahim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, that Ali (peace be upon him) said:
"Whoever feeds children and adults in expiation for an oath, he must provide for the child an amount equal to what the adult ate."
ai.seo_question: What is the required amount of food for a child in the expiation of an oath compared to an adult?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies a specific jurisprudential detail regarding the expiation (kaffarah) of an oath, mandating that the food portion for a child must equal that of an adult, contrary to the general principle of proportional distribution. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise equity in ritual obligations, ensuring that the spiritual merit of the expiation is not diminished by the recipient's age or capacity. It reflects the broader Imami legal tradition of deriving nuanced practical applications from the general injunctions found in the Quran.
